cultural.vision_reason: A classic strip-woven kente cloth in vivid multicolour geometric pattern, hand-woven and hand-sewn — the signature textile of the Ashanti (Akan) people of Ghana.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular woman’s wrapper composed of 12 hand-woven narrow strips of imported European cotton and rayon in an unusually wide range of colours, which have been hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are designed and assembled to form a chequerboard pattern; both ends have a variant design of five bands of weft blocks that serve as a border to the main field. There are six different warp designs on the strips (one of them being the oyokoman design); these are repeated over each half of the cloth but in a different order. The weft designs are equally varied: there is no standard pattern wither for the pairs of end blocks, or for the supplementary patterns between them. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.
